text.p: Juventus may be the Italian league leaders and 17 points ahead of 13th-placed Napoli but they will still be wary of the Naples side when they meet at the San Paolo stadium on Sunday.
Experienced Juventus defender Ciro Ferrara, for 10 seasons a Napoli player, has no doubt that his old club will offer stiff opposition.
"This is a difficult game for us, I'd say our most difficult away fixture from now to the end of the season," Ferrara said.
"If I'm not mistaken only Inter have managed to win at the San Paolo this year".
Napoli goalkeeper Giuseppe Taglialatela is an old friend of Ferrara and usually phones him before they meet in a match.
This week, however, the Napoli goalkeeper has opted not to phone his rival.
"I rang him before all the other games but we never won. Let's see how it works out this time even if I know only too well that superstitions are not enough...to guarantee a win."
An expected full house of more than 75,000 spectators will generate a $1.3-million gate receipt on Sunday.
In the past, this was a game which brought together the exotic skills of Napoli's Argentine Diego Maradona and Juventus's French ace Michel Platini in a clash often decisive for the title contest.
This time the title is not at stake but Neapolitan pride is at a club unsettled by the news that coach Luigi Simoni will be leaving at the end of the season.
Juventus come into the game five points clear of second-placed Parma, with Sampdoria a further four points back in third.
Juventus, who defeated Norway's Rosenborg 2-0 in midweek to qualify for a European Cup semifinal clash with Ajax Amsterdam, have doubts about their attack.
Alessandro Del Piero is still out through injury and the club is appealing against the two-match suspension of their Croatian striker Alen Boksic, who has already sat out one league fixture.
Further complications concern Christian Vieri who twisted an ankle against Rosenborg and may be replaced by Michele Padovano alongside Nicola Amoruso.
Alessio Tacchinardi comes in to the Juventus midfield in place of suspended Yugoslav Vladimir Jugovic.
Napoli may also be without Brazilian Andre Cruz and Frenchman Alain Boghossian, both injured.
In their absence, Fabio Pecchi and Brazilian Beto play in midfield while Alfredo Aglietti and Nicola Caccia lead the attack.
Recent tradition is against Napoli since they last won this home tie in September 1990.
